text: Then the cavalry arrives. A Gate Rescue van smashes through the enclosure gate, police cars right behind it.
Choi leaps out with a megaphone. An unregistered gate is Gate Rescue's by law, so nobody moves.
The Kanghan guards look at each other, and lower their batons.
Yerin sprints across the mud with her first-aid bag, Bomi right behind her.
Yerin's healing closes Jaeha's cuts. But his hands won't stop shaking. They will, he says. Can she hold his phone?
She holds it to his ear, his trembling fingers on her wrist.
It's Seoa, furious. What is o? Is he alive? He is. He'll be home for dinner. Seven o'clock.
Responders hand out foil blankets, police tape off the steel plate, and the summons sit together by Borro.
Uncle Pyo grips Jaeha's shaking hand. Ten years, and the first time he's come out of a gate as a person.
Moon Ahin gives Choi her phone. Her face is on it. They can't bury her face. Watch them try, says Choi.
Alone in the van, Choi copies the video onto an old USB stick.
Then he tucks the stick between two rolls of kimbap.
Nobody in this country, Choi reasons, has ever stolen a man's kimbap.
At dawn they sit in a long row on the riverbank, in foil blankets. Everyone came back. Every single one.
Moon Ahin asks what you name something you don't want to lose. Whatever it already is, says Jaeha. You just have to notice.
She looks at her lead husk, standing alone against the sunrise. Saebyeok. Dawn. His name is Saebyeok.
Nine in the morning. Choi hands the evidence to Inspector Ryu, who promises it won't leave his hands.
Then Deputy Director Hwang steps in, smiling. A matter this sensitive goes straight to his office.
Ryu lets go of the bag. He doesn't look happy about it.
At four that afternoon, everyone crowds into the Gate Rescue break room to watch the Association's press conference.
Hwang, sorrowful at the podium. The footage is inconclusive, maybe staged. The witnesses are day labourers, unreliable. Insufficient evidence.
Ho throws his cup at the wall. Uncle Pyo doesn't move. Ten years, and the word is unreliable.
Jaeha's eyes narrow at the screen.
As Hwang turns away, his lapel flips over, and underneath is a small silver hexagon pin.
Jaeha has Bomi pause it. The same hexagon as the tanks. The deputy director, sighs Choi. Of course.
Bomi jumps up. Let her post the video to her million subscribers. Let them bury that!
Jaeha shakes his head. Tonight they'd call it fake and sue the one person whose face is in it. It has to stick.
Choi pats his kimbap box. When the time comes, it's right here, with the tuna ones.
Lyra perks up at the word tuna. Is it for sharing?
Jaeha's coffee trembles in rings, and slops onto his knee.
Yerin watches his hands, and says nothing.
Earlier that afternoon, Moon Ahin strides through Kanghan Tower in a fresh white coat, hair loose, past bowing secretaries, and furious.
Her uncle, Director Baek Taegun, turns from the window. Is she hurt? Her mother was worried sick.
Very quietly, she says it. He knew. The giant, the pipes, her grandfather's seal on the glass.
Baek rests a hand on the glass case of his core. Half of Seoul's hospitals run on their cores, down to the incubators.
Then he looks at her, gentle and kind. Does she want the hospitals dark, Ahin?
She has no answer. The baton trembles at her side.
The Association found nothing, he says. It's over. Dinner on Sunday. Her mother misses her.
She walks to the door without a word.
At the door, she stops. His name is Saebyeok. Whose? Her first husk. Her uncle taught her not to name them.
The door clicks shut, and one eyebrow lifts behind his glasses.
Five forty, the columbarium. Jaeha walks the long white corridor alone, Minseok's rusted lamp in his hand.
He sets the lamp on the ledge beside Choi's can of coffee, his hands trembling.
He found his hyung's door, he tells the photo, and the giant. Minseok wasn't alone. And Jaeha is going back for him. He promised.
Behind the glass, Minseok grins, thumb up.
Then Jaeha checks the time and hurries off. Sorry, hyung. He promised Seoa dinner at seven, and he's always late.
At dusk, Han Sora lounges in a sports car on an overpass, boots on the dash, wrist bandaged. Her phone buzzes.
Good evening, Director. Before he asks: yes, she lost his compass.
Baek stands alone at his window as the city lights up. Tell him how.
Sora is delighted all over again. The Operator moved her needle, and his archer shot it off her wrist without touching her. On purpose.
Did he kill anyone?
For once, Sora isn't smiling. Not one. He carried his rival's husks, all of them. And his body is breaking. She saw his hands.
Baek's hand tightens on his cane.
So, does she go and collect him, while he can't hold a chopstick?
Baek's eyes behind his glasses, the city lights in the lenses.
No. Don't touch the Operator.
Then what, Sora asks.
And for the first time, Baek's polite smile reaches its full width. Make him come to us.
Across the city in Mangwon, warm bulbs light a small rooftop. A table is set, and one figure in a hoodie hurries up the stairs.
